verdict.rationale: The evidence shows only narrow pieces of this story. The iOS SDK's appHangCallback lets developers add diagnostic context, such as the current screen, when an app hang is detected. The Correlated Events feature implies events carry user, device, session and trace attributes. Nothing documents breadcrumbs or custom tags/metadata being attached to every event across SDKs. missing for 10: documented breadcrumbs API, custom tags/metadata on all events, explicit developer-set user context API, cross-platform coverage beyond iOS app hangs, independent/hands-on corroboration

support.subject: As a developer, I can attach breadcrumbs, custom tags, and user context to every event so a stack trace arrives with the state that produced it

citations.quote: The new appHangCallback in the BugSnag iOS SDK lets you add diagnostic context, such as the current screen or how many assets are still loading, the moment an app hang is detected.
Instantly see related BugSnag events sharing the same user, device, session, or trace
